svg.title: Receive scheduling: fixed CTA roles or warp Round Robin
svg.desc: Fixed scheduling assigns CTAs zero to 255 to relay draining and CTAs 256 to 383 to final copying. Round Robin gives every warp static source/send-CTA tasks, probes readiness and cooperatively executes one ready stage at a time. Both schedules accept Direct and hierarchical sources. The representative Round Robin warp zero has lane zero assigned remote source zero/send CTA zero and lane one assigned local source eight/send CTA zero.
svg.text: Two incoming jobs. Two alternative schedules. One compatible protocol.
Fixed receive
Warp Round Robin
Dedicated CTA ranges run concurrently
All 384 CTAs · 8 warps per CTA in this example
CTAs 0–255 · hierReceiveRelay
Visit remote source/send-CTA tasks in order
Relay staging → LSA copies into final slots → done
Direct sources have no remote relay payload to drain.
CTAs 256–383 · hierReceiveFinal
Acquire completion for this GPU’s final slots
Internal final slots → recv_x + receive metadata
Accept Direct, relayed, and source-local arrivals.
Unique task ownership; separate relay and final-copy workers.
Representative warp 0 on receiving GPU 10
Lane 0: remote source 0 / send CTA 0
Lane 1: local source 8 / send CTA 0
hierProbeReceiveTask + warp ballots
Skip unready tasks; rotate among ready stages
Whole warp executes the selected stage
Relay forwarding OR final-slot copying
Static task set per warp; no work stealing.
Receive schedule uses capacity/configuration, not the rank’s current outgoing token count.
Each source’s publication and completion determine what work actually exists.
Same-grid comparison: capacity 512, 384 logical CTAs. A qualifying EP16/H7168/K6-or-K8 configuration uses Round Robin.
